title: MirrorGeometryNode socket docs: warn about symmetric-input non-manifold
description: Applying mirror_geometry to input geometry that is ALREADY symmetric across the mirror plane (e.g. a stock cube centered at origin, mirrored on X) produces overlapping faces that merge_by_distance collapses into a non-manifold topology. The mesh validates, probe fails at execution. A role-play session today hit exactly this: cube(size=1) is symmetric, and mirror_geometry(axis=X) on it crashed mesh execution. Fix: update MirrorGeometryNode.socketDocs for the 'geometry' port to warn: 'INPUT MUST NOT ALREADY BE SYMMETRIC across the mirror plane — mirroring an already-symmetric shape produces overlapping faces that collapse into non-manifold edges. Build a half-shape (e.g. cube shifted to x in [0, 1]) first, then mirror.'
definition-of-done: 1. MirrorGeometryNode.socketDocs for 'geometry' includes the symmetric-input warning. 2. Catalog regeneration shows the warning. 3. Next interactive session picks a half-shape strategy on first try.
testing-plan: 1. Regenerate catalog. 2. Grep mesh-node-catalog.json for 'already-symmetric' near mirror_geometry. 3. Render the system prompt and verify the warning appears under mirror_geometry's geometry port.
